定音鼓具有深沉、宏亮且富有力度的音色特徵。其音色質感介於明亮與暗沉之間，帶有溫厚: The timpani has a deep, resonant, forceful timbre. Its tone sits between bright and dark, with a warm resonance; a stroke gives a clear attack and then a deep drum sound. The range covers the low and middle registers, with a wide span of adjustable pitch, since the tension of the head can be changed to set the pitch precisely. Its way of resonating is distinctive: the vibration of the head is transmitted into the body of the drum to make a thick, penetrating sound. Compared with the soft, long lines of the strings, the timpani is more direct and forceful; compared with the brass cymbals, it is deeper and lacks their bright shimmer. In a symphony orchestra the timpani often reinforces the bass foundation, giving the whole band rhythmic and dynamic support.
定音鼓是中東／歐洲的膜鳴樂器，其聆聽場合以合奏編制為主：它由軍鼓演變而來，巴洛克: The timpani is a membranophone from the Middle East / Europe, and it is heard mainly in ensemble line-ups: it developed from the military drum, entered the orchestra in the late Baroque, became a standard orchestral instrument in the Classical period, and today appears in symphony orchestras, wind bands and marching bands, as well as in some rock bands. Pedal timpani are mostly used by orchestras in fixed venues, while marching timpani are slung on a strap across the chest and are common in European and American marching bands. For specific pieces, listen to Darius Milhaud's 《La création du monde》 and timpani works by Ney Rosauro, William Kraft, Mitchell Peters and John Beck.
定音鼓源自古代戰爭戰鼓，七世紀文獻已見其名，西班牙神學家聖依西多祿《詞源》提及。: The timpani descends from the war drums of antiquity; the name appears in seventh-century documents, and the Spanish theologian Isidore of Seville mentions it in his 《Etymologiae》. It later evolved from the military drum, entered the orchestra in the late Baroque and became a standard orchestral instrument in the Classical period. Mechanical tuning appeared in the nineteenth century, and modern pedal timpani can change pitch quickly and accurately; they are used in symphony orchestras, wind bands, marching bands and some rock bands.

Hand-tuned drums need the six to eight bolts around the rim tightened one by one to change the tension of the head; mechanical drums change the tension by turning a handle; pedal drums use a foot pedal to work a linkage and tune quickly and accurately. With a ratchet clutch, the player has to disengage the clutch before pressing the pedal to tune, re-engage it when the target pitch is reached, and then fine-tune with the adjusting handle. Marching timpani can be slung on a strap across the chest and played.
定音鼓的鼓身傳統上以銅製成，較廉價型號則使用玻璃纖維或鋁。鼓面為單面膜，可為獸皮: The bowl of a timpani is traditionally copper; cheaper models use fibreglass or aluminium. The head is a single membrane, either animal skin, commonly calfskin or goatskin, or a plastic film; plastic heads are more durable, weather-resistant and cheaper, while skin heads sound warmer. The head is fixed in a hoop and tensioned with tuning screws, and the tuning mechanism may be cast metal or a metal linkage. Mallet shafts are mostly hardwood or bamboo, sometimes aluminium or carbon fibre; the heads are usually felt over a wooden core, and there are also compressed felt, cork or leather cores.

The timpani is a membranophone in the percussion family, Hornbostel–Sachs classification 211.11-922. It is a head stretched over a hemispherical copper bowl, made of animal skin or plastic film, with a pedal mechanism that changes the tension of the head so that the player can change pitch quickly while playing. It is played with a pair of timpani mallets on the head. The timpani evolved from ancient war drums and is now common in symphony orchestras, concert wind bands, marching bands and some rock bands, and is played by a timpanist.
